upstream.scope: A typed server-side metric catalogue for the fields srtop already publishes (process PID, name, resident memory and CPU; the seven PX-007 system-summary figures), one availability vocabulary, and an on-demand collection policy for expensive fields proven with scripted sources; no new metric family, no production expensive field, no change to any published cell, heading or summary line, no htop parity claim

entries.feature: Every published field is one typed catalogue entry: stable dotted key, unit, §6.5 raw type (unsigned integer, string or small typed record), origin, aggregation semantics (none, sum, non-additive), default formatter and typed sort, required capability, sensitivity, collection cost and supported refresh tiers; the four process columns and seven system-summary figures are catalogued and the table's headings and row cells are built from the same catalogued column list, with every heading, cell and summary line unchanged
entries.scope: PX-042/apps/srtop server-side catalogue; fake, scripted and live procfs sources unchanged in output

entries.feature: The catalogue refuses a malformed key, a duplicate key, more than its entry bound, and every incompatible unit: a definition whose unit text names another unit, a raw type, formatter, aggregation or sort that does not fit the unit; it refuses an expensive or process-content field that claims every-sample collection, a field with no or repeated tiers, and a host-wide field offered on demand
entries.scope: PX-042/catalogue validation, unit tests with deliberate one-change refusals

entries.feature: One availability vocabulary — present, warming up, permission denied, unsupported, stale and failed — distinct for every field, with only present carrying a quantity; the existing per-field states (Observed, CpuUsage, FigureGap, SystemCpu) map onto it and each non-present state's word is exactly the cell the field already publishes
entries.scope: PX-042/process and system fields; no published wording changed

entries.feature: Expensive fields are collected only on demand for the selected or visible rows that ask for them: hidden fields are forgotten and never read, sampled or uncatalogued fields are refused rather than polled, tracked fields and outstanding reads are bounded, dispatch goes to never-read fields and then the oldest reading so no demanded field starves, every read answers (a panicking or dropped read fails its field and frees its slot; a hung read is given up at its deadline; a field never has more than one read outstanding, in flight or given up, across hide and re-show (a re-shown field adopts its in-flight read, and a given-up field is not read again until that read returns); and reads in flight plus given up never exceed a fixed bound; if that many distinct fields wedge, collection pauses with stale or failed states, never warming up indefinitely, while a field merely queued behind healthy reads stays warming up, and resumes when any returns; limits that would let nothing be dispatched are refused), reads run on the runtime's blocking pool so a blocked read leaves the sample loop publishing, an older completion never replaces a newer result, and each value carries the start time of its read on a monotonic clock that counts host suspend, is failed if stamped outside its request-to-drain window, and is stale rather than present once older than its freshness bound
entries.scope: PX-042/on-demand policy proven with scripted expensive fields, a manual clock and a manual dispatcher; no production expensive field exists, and no selection or visible-range signal drives it yet
